title: kit.staleness-registry.v1
description: packages/core/registry/staleness.json: the names `kit check staleness` reads (docs/FRESHNESS.md): the remote and branch whose live head every local branch must contain, the directories whose JSON registries carry dated facts, the site's release file and the path every Worker answers its commit on, and the file that publishes the kit's head. One source: nothing else names them.

worktree_registry.description: Where `kit check staleness --local` reads the worktree registry (kit.worktrees.v1), relative to the directory it runs in.

scratch_max_age_days.description: The oldest an entry of the scratch directory may be (scratch-aged).

scratch_env.description: The environment variable that names the machine's scratch directory (the worktree registry's `scratch` is the fallback); the working directory is never the scratch directory.

scratch_walk.description: The bound of the walk that finds the newest file of a scratch entry: a tree larger than this cannot be aged and is an unreadable finding, never a guess.

verification_days.description: The property names that hold the day a fact was read from its source. `kit check staleness` judges each against max_age_days; finding class verified-without-max-age requires the same names to sit beside a max_age_days in a schema (a test proves the two lists are one).

deploy_paths_always.description: The files and directories that deploy whatever the Workers' configs say (the lockfile, the release file, the vendored kit). The Workers' own deployable paths are derived from the release Workers' wrangler configs, entry files and migrations directories (one source); release.json `paths` replaces both.
